correctness.rationale: The boundary criterion is correct. If positive labels occur in both \(A_p\) and \(B_1\), every positive \(A\)-vertex sees the positive \(B_1\) vertex and every positive \(B\)-vertex sees the positive \(A_p\) vertex. Conversely, if \(B_1\) is all zero, Roman domination forces every \(A_1\) vertex positive, but those vertices then have only zero neighbors; the argument is symmetric for \(A_p\). Conditioning the already-correct Roman classwise enumeration on those two positivity requirements yields the displayed factors. A fresh independent five-vertex chain-graph enumeration in this audit checked the criterion for every \(3^5\) labeling and obtained minimum weight four; the frozen verifier checks all canonical profiles through order nine.
correctness.risk: No correctness issue was found; rejection is solely for prior implication and value.

originality.rationale: Two already-published chain-graph results jointly imply the submitted theorem. The published Roman-domination-polynomial record classifies every Roman dominating function using exactly the same extremal indices and local factors. The published total-and-connected-total-domination record proves that a vertex subset of a connected chain graph is total dominating exactly when it meets \(A_p\) and \(B_1\). For any Roman dominating function, its positive support already dominates every zero vertex via a label-2 neighbor; therefore the function is total Roman exactly when that positive support is a total dominating set. Combining the two prior theorems gives the submitted boundary criterion immediately, and the new polynomial is the prior Roman polynomial with the two extreme-class positivity filters inserted.
